\section[o fogo de artifício]{o fogo de artifício — the fireworks}

\label{lesson:PT-C322-fogo-de-artificio}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Portuguese for the disguise, then the Portuguese for to disguise.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: o fogo de artifício}
\textbf{o fogo de artifício} — \textquotedblleft{}the fireworks\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
À meia-noite houve fogo de artifício na praia.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{At midnight there were fireworks on the beach.}
\end{quote}

Singular in Portuguese: \emph{o fogo de artifício foi lindo}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{fogo} is inherited from Latin \emph{focus} \textquotedblleft{}a hearth\textquotedblright{} (EtymDB); \emph{artifício} is a learned borrowing from Latin \emph{artificium} \textquotedblleft{}a craft, a skill\textquotedblright{}, built on \emph{ars} \textquotedblleft{}art\textquotedblright{} (Lewis \& Short).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}

  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Portuguese for the disguise, then the Portuguese for to disguise, then say \emph{o fogo de artifício} again

\section[o foguete]{o foguete — the rocket}

\label{lesson:PT-C322-foguete}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Portuguese for to disguise, then the Portuguese for the fireworks.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: o foguete}
\textbf{o foguete} — \textquotedblleft{}the rocket\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
Um foguete subiu e explodiu no céu.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{A rocket went up and burst in the sky.}
\end{quote}

Also a space rocket. At village festivals, \emph{foguetes} are fired to announce the party.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{foguete} is a little \emph{fogo} \textquotedblleft{}fire\textquotedblright{} (EtymDB lists it), from Latin \emph{focus} \textquotedblleft{}a hearth\textquotedblright{}, with the small-thing ending \emph{-ete}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Portuguese for to disguise, then the Portuguese for the fireworks, then say \emph{o foguete} again

\section[a fogueira]{a fogueira — the bonfire}

\label{lesson:PT-C322-fogueira}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Portuguese for the fireworks, then the Portuguese for the rocket.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: a fogueira}
\textbf{a fogueira} — \textquotedblleft{}the bonfire\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
Na praia, fizemos uma fogueira e cantámos.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{On the beach we made a bonfire and sang.}
\end{quote}

People jump over \emph{fogueiras} on some June nights.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{fogueira} comes down from Old Portuguese (EtymDB) and goes back to Vulgar Latin \emph{focāria}, built on Latin \emph{focus} \textquotedblleft{}a hearth\textquotedblright{}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\section[enfeitar]{enfeitar — to decorate, to adorn}

\label{lesson:PT-C322-enfeitar}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Portuguese for the rocket, then the Portuguese for the bonfire.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: enfeitar}
\textbf{enfeitar} — \textquotedblleft{}to decorate, to adorn\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
As crianças enfeitaram a sala com balões.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{The children decorated the room with balloons.}
\end{quote}

\emph{Enfeitar-se} — to dress up, to make oneself pretty.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{enfeitar} is usually traced to \emph{en-} and \emph{feito} \textquotedblleft{}made\textquotedblright{}, the past participle of \emph{fazer}, from Latin \emph{factus} (Lewis \& Short); EtymDB has the word with no source.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\section[o enfeite]{o enfeite — the decoration, the ornament}

\label{lesson:PT-C322-enfeite}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Portuguese for the bonfire, then the Portuguese for to decorate.

\subsection*{You'll want to know: o enfeite}
\textbf{o enfeite} — \textquotedblleft{}the decoration, the ornament\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
Ela fez um enfeite de papel para a janela.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{She made a paper decoration for the window.}
\end{quote}

Built on \emph{enfeitar}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{enfeite} is built on \emph{enfeitar} \textquotedblleft{}to decorate\textquotedblright{}, which is usually traced to \emph{en-} and \emph{feito} \textquotedblleft{}made\textquotedblright{}, from Latin \emph{factus} (Lewis \& Short).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
